options.name: Kirbyville church yards (ask permission)
options.priceNote: Free with permission; Southern Tier tradition — 'many riders stay at the church in Kirbyville' (Helder ST notes). Kirbyville Methodist, 105 W Main St; First Baptist, 105 N Barrow Ave.
options.locationNote: In town, blocks from endpoint. Coordinates approximate (Methodist church).
options.legalityNote: Legal only with explicit permission from church staff — call or knock before pitching. Do not set up unannounced.
options.cyclistIntel: David Helder's Southern Tier notes say many riders overnight at the church in Kirbyville before the DeRidder leg; a Warm Showers host (Debbie) south of town also hosted riders in 2014 journals. Kirbyville has a small motel + groceries.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round; October evenings mild.

options.name: Merryville Museum cyclist camp (Burk's Cabin grounds)
options.priceNote: Free/donation — museum members are 'proud hosts' of Southern Tier cyclists; small cabin (fold-out bed, AC, fridge, charging) or tent on grounds. Confirm donation amount when calling.
options.locationNote: 628 N Railroad Ave, Merryville LA — ~20 route miles BEHIND the Kirbyville endpoint, before the Sabine crossing. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Established cyclist hosting by the museum; fully sanctioned. Beauregard Tourism also lists a cyclists camping site at the Atakapa-Coushatta Trace Visitors Center, 703 N Bryan St.
options.cyclistIntel: Well-known lower-Southern-Tier stop; hosts guided ACA groups and solo riders. Cafe in town praised in journals.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round.

options.name: Magnolia Ridge Park (USACE, B.A. Steinhagen Lake)
options.priceNote: $10/night tent non-electric; $18-20 electric. 50% off with federal Senior/Access pass.
options.locationNote: Off US 190 near Woodville — roughly 28-30 miles NORTH of Kirbyville via Jasper, well outside the normal flex window. Only viable if deliberately rerouting via US 190. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Established Corps of Engineers campground, 41 reservable sites, open year-round.
options.cyclistIntel: Cheap and quiet, but the detour makes it impractical for the standard ACA routing — listed for completeness.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; October availability is easy midweek.

gapAdvice: No verified campground exists in or near Kirbyville itself. Plan A: call the Kirbyville Methodist/Baptist churches a day ahead (long-standing rider tradition). Plan B: stop 20 mi early at the Merryville Museum cyclist camp (free, cabin possible) and ride a longer Day 13. Plan C: Kirbyville's small motel. Check Warmshowers for the Kirbyville-area host seen in journals.

options.name: Big Thicket National Preserve backcountry (Turkey Creek unit)
options.priceNote: Free backcountry permit, issued in person at the visitor center same-day or up to 14 days ahead.
options.locationNote: Visitor center at US 69/FM 420, ~7 mi north of Kountze (coordinates = visitor center; camp along Turkey Creek Trail 200 ft off trail). Off the westbound route direction.
options.legalityNote: Legal ONLY with the free permit; camp 200+ ft from trails/roads/water (or on Village Creek sandbars within 25 ft of water); no campfires; pack out trash.
options.cyclistIntel: Workable for a self-sufficient rider but logistically clunky: permit pickup requires reaching the visitor center during open hours, then hiking gear in. Carry all water.
options.seasonalNote: Oct 1-Feb 28 hunting season limits camping to non-hunted areas — Turkey Creek, Village Creek Corridor, and Neches River Corridor units remain open year-round; Oct 3 is day 3 of that restriction.

options.name: Village Creek State Park (Creekside hike-in sites)
options.priceNote: $10/night hike-in primitive site + $4/person daily entrance fee (TPWD entry is extra, per person 13+). Electric sites $16 + entry.
options.locationNote: Lumberton, ~6 mi south of Silsbee off US 96 — leave the route around mile 737 before the final leg into Kountze (~10 mi east of the Kountze endpoint).
options.legalityNote: TPWD state park; 15 hike-in sites with water nearby, restrooms with showers in park.
options.cyclistIntel: The reliable legal-camping anchor for the Big Thicket day; several ST journals detour here rather than overnight in Kountze proper.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; October midweek availability good.

options.name: Indian Springs Camp
options.priceNote: Tent rate not published — estimate $15-25; call to confirm.
options.locationNote: 6106 Holland Cemetery Rd, Kountze — on Village Creek roughly 4-5 mi southeast of the Kountze endpoint. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Established private camp with dedicated tent and wilderness camping areas; baths/showers near tent area.
options.cyclistIntel: Canoe/kayak outfitter camp on Village Creek; quiet on October weekdays.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round; call ahead — office hours vary.

options.name: Big Thicket Hideaway Campground
options.priceNote: RV sites from $35; tent rate unlisted — likely $20-30, call to confirm.
options.locationNote: 5539 FM 420, Kountze — ~6 mi north of town near the Big Thicket visitor center. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Private campground advertising tent camping, showers, laundry, WiFi.
options.cyclistIntel: Convenient pairing with a Big Thicket visitor-center stop; north-of-town location adds miles.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round.

options.name: Red Cloud RV Park
options.priceNote: Published nightly $50-60 all-inclusive appears to be the RV rate; tents accepted — call for tent price (may be less). Over budget if quoted RV rate.
options.locationNote: 2351 US 96 N, Silsbee — essentially on-route (OSM pegs it at mile 733.2), ~13 mi before Kountze. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Commercial RV park with tent sites, bath house, laundry.
options.cyclistIntel: On-route convenience is its only edge; mostly long-term residents per reviews.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round.

bestBet: Village Creek State Park (Creekside hike-in sites)

options.name: Lone Star Hiking Trail designated hiker camps (Big Woods/Magnolia sections)
options.priceNote: Free; no permit needed.
options.locationNote: Primitive designated camps along the LSHT near Double Lake/Big Creek Scenic Area, ~1-3 mi off route on foot paths. Coordinates approximate — use the LSHT Club map for exact camp locations.
options.legalityNote: During hunting season (2025-26 policy: Sept 20-Jan 25; expect same window for 2026-27, covering Oct 4) SHNF camping is restricted to DESIGNATED sites — these hiker camps are the designated ones, so they stay legal. Wear orange.
options.cyclistIntel: Fire ring/tent pad only; no water — tank up in Coldspring. Verify trail-section status with the ranger district: the 2024 flood closure order (expired June 1, 2026) had closed the whole LSHT and some sections may still be under repair.
options.seasonalNote: Designated-camping-only period assumed in effect early Oct 2026; confirm 2026-27 dates at lonestartrail.org.

options.name: Double Lake Recreation Area (Sam Houston NF)
options.priceNote: $20/night tent non-electric single site (recreation.gov); day use $7/vehicle — walk/bike-in day use $1/person.
options.locationNote: 1.4 mi off route at day's end (OSM mile 817.6), just south of Coldspring.
options.legalityNote: Developed 1937 CCC campground, 43 sites (10 tent-only), flush toilets, bathhouse with concession; also first-come if sites open. No arrivals 10pm-6am.
options.cyclistIntel: The obvious anchor for this day. IMPORTANT: it was on the 2024 flood closure list, but that order expired June 1, 2026 and the FS page now shows it OPEN (swim beach open since Apr 30) — still worth a confirming call since forest repairs are ongoing.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; verified open as of Aug 2026. Reserve on recreation.gov — October weekdays wide open.

bestBet: Double Lake Recreation Area (Sam Houston NF)

options.name: Kelly's Pond Campground (Sam Houston NF)
options.priceNote: Camping is FREE (FS-confirmed); $5/person/day only if using the motorized trail system.
options.locationNote: End of FSR 271, ~2.7 mi east of the day's endpoint (OSM hint). Gravel access road.
options.legalityNote: Official FS campground: 8 primitive walk-in tent sites with tables, fire rings, lantern posts, vault toilets. FS page (Aug 2026): 'Dispersed Camping and Day Use are open.' Counts as a designated site during the hunting-season camping restriction.
options.cyclistIntel: NO potable water — load up in Montgomery (3 mi). Popular with OHV riders on weekends, but Oct 5, 2026 is a Monday, so expect quiet. Cheapest legal bed on this whole segment.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; confirmed open post-flood-closure (order expired June 1, 2026).

options.name: Little Lake Creek Wilderness / LSHT designated hiker camp
options.priceNote: Free; no permit.
options.locationNote: OSM shows a wilderness camp 0.9 mi off route near the endpoint (west side, LSHT western terminus area). Coordinates approximate — verify against LSHT Club map.
options.legalityNote: Legal in Oct 2026 ONLY at designated hiker/hunter camps (hunting-season policy, ~Sept 20-Jan 25); random dispersed spots are off-limits in that window. Wear orange.
options.cyclistIntel: Pure primitive — fire ring/tent pad at best, no water. Bikes not allowed on wilderness trail tread; you'd walk the bike or camp at a trailhead-adjacent designated site. Kelly's Pond is easier logistics for the same $0.
options.seasonalNote: Confirm LSHT section status post-2024-flood repairs with the district office.

options.name: Lake Conroe / Houston North KOA Holiday
options.priceNote: ~$52/night average for premium tent sites (water, electric, fire pit); 20% weeknight discount Sun-Thu can pull it near $40. Over budget — fallback only.
options.locationNote: 19785 TX-105 W, Montgomery — ~3.4 mi off route per OSM hint. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Commercial KOA; tents explicitly welcome.
options.cyclistIntel: Hot showers, laundry, pool — a comfort splurge if the free NF options feel too rough after four camp nights.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round.

options.name: Lake Somerville State Park - Nails Creek Unit
options.priceNote: $12/night water-only site + $5/person daily entrance fee (TPWD entry extra). Electric $20 + entry.
options.locationNote: Off FM 180 on the lake's southwest arm — ~8 mi north of the route near Burton (route mile ~944), ~15 total flex miles past Gay Hill.
options.legalityNote: TPWD state park; restrooms with showers; primitive Trailway sites also available.
options.cyclistIntel: Cheapest verified option on Somerville Lake, but the farthest pedal; only worth it if you're pushing past Gay Hill anyway.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round; October availability good midweek.

options.name: Yegua Creek Park (USACE, Somerville Lake)
options.priceNote: $20/night non-electric tent site; $26 tent site with 30A electric (2025 Corps rate sheet). Federal Senior/Access pass halves it to $10.
options.locationNote: 12563 Yegua Creek Park Rd, Burton — south shore below the dam, ~3 mi off route per OSM hint (route mile ~940 between Gay Hill and Burton). Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Corps campground, open YEAR-ROUND, gated 6am-10pm; flush toilets, showers, water at sites.
options.cyclistIntel: The classic cheap-with-showers Corps stop for this day; October weekday sites plentiful on recreation.gov (also bookable at 1-877-444-6777).
options.seasonalNote: Year-round per Corps park list — no October closure.

options.name: Rocky Creek Park (USACE, Somerville Lake)
options.priceNote: Tent-only sites all have 20/30A electric + water — from $26/night (no cheaper non-electric tier here).
options.locationNote: 10550 Rocky Creek Park Rd, Burton — south shore ~3 mi west of Yegua Creek, ~4-5 mi off route. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Corps campground, year-round, 192 sites incl. 35 tent-only; showers, restrooms.
options.cyclistIntel: Backup if Yegua Creek is full (unlikely in October); slightly pricier since every site is electric.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round.

options.name: Overlook Park & Marina (private)
options.priceNote: Tent rate not published — estimate $25-35; call to confirm.
options.locationNote: 505 Marina Rd, Brenham — east shore near the dam, ~3-4 mi off route. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Private marina campground with tent camping and a modern bathhouse (this is the 'Overlook Park' in OSM — it is NOT a free Corps day-use park).
options.cyclistIntel: Nicest bathhouse on the lake per reviews; Brenham (~8 mi off route) remains the motel fallback.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round.

options.name: Buescher State Park (Oak Haven / Lakeview / primitive walk-in)
options.priceNote: $15/night water-only tent site (Lakeview #41-60) or $15 primitive walk-in (#61-65, first-come) + $5/person daily entrance fee (TPWD entry extra). Electric (Oak Haven/Cozy Circle) $18 + entry.
options.locationNote: Park camping loops are 0.1 mi off the route at the day's endpoint — the OSM 'Oak Haven', 'Cozy Circle', and 'Lakeview' camps ARE Buescher SP's camping areas.
options.legalityNote: TPWD state park; restrooms with showers near Lakeview and the electric loops; primitive sites #61-65 are no-reservation first-come.
options.cyclistIntel: Ends the day literally at the park gate; Smithville groceries/cafes 2 mi south. Reserve online for the water/electric sites, or roll in for a first-come primitive pad.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round; October is prime season here but weekdays are fine.

options.name: Vernon L. Richards Riverbend Park (City of Smithville)
options.priceNote: $20/night (holiday weekends higher); all 19 paved sites have electricity, tables, grills, fire rings; tents allowed.
options.locationNote: On TX-71 at the Colorado River on Smithville's north edge, ~1-2 mi off the endpoint. Coordinates approximate.
options.legalityNote: Official city park camping; NO on-site office — reserve by phoning the City Recreation Center Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30 (Oct 7, 2026 is a Wednesday, so call that week). Showers not confirmed — restrooms only per city page.
options.cyclistIntel: Cyclists and event campers use it regularly (hosts bike rallies); day use is free. Same price as Buescher but with electricity and no entry fee.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round.

options.name: Bastrop State Park
options.priceNote: $15/night water-only tent site (Deer Run, tents only) or $15 walk-in Creekside site + daily entrance fee (~$6/person — confirm). Electric $20, full hookup $25.
options.locationNote: ~12 route miles PAST Smithville toward Bastrop (mile ~1016) — an overshoot option that shortens Day 18.
options.legalityNote: TPWD state park; tent areas have water nearby, restrooms/showers in camp loops.
options.cyclistIntel: Classic ST stop in the Lost Pines; note the historic Park Road 1C connector from Buescher to Bastrop is a beautiful but hilly ride.
options.seasonalNote: Year-round; entrance fee amount not verified on the fetched page — budget ~$6/person.

bestBet: Buescher State Park (Oak Haven / Lakeview / primitive walk-in)
